literature.headline_zh: Wolbachia蚊与微流控技术并进:本周登革热研究与防控新动向。
literature.lead_zh: 本周多篇登革热研究覆盖媒介生物防控、预测模型、临床生物标志物、疫苗免疫学及快速诊断技术。一项荟萃分析显示全区域释放Wolbachia蚊可使发病率下降约85%;微流控与RT-LAMP等快速检测工具持续优化,以支持资源有限地区的现场分型需求。
key_findings_zh: Wolbachia蚊全区域释放与登革热发病率显著下降相关,合并IRR为0.15(95%CI 0.05–0.39),对应估计下降85% [10.1093/trstmh/trag063]。
在泄漏安全的时间序列设计中,基于监测数据的LSTM模型在2025年外部时间验证中表现最佳,MAE为7.951,R2为0.698 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10307931/v1]。
泰国2005–2024年监测显示25岁以上成人病例占比从19.56%升至36.16%,Kitagawa分解提示主要驱动力为流行病学因素而非人口老龄化 [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014697]。
印度尼西亚坦格朗县全年监测中DENV-2占比32.8%,继发感染与重症显著相关(调整后OR=10.25,95%CI 1.71–197.90) [10.7883/yoken.jjid.2025.232]。
针对四价血清型的双重读出RT-LAMP在斯里兰卡临床样本中DENV-1/2/3检出率分别为91.2%、78.6%、100%,且无血清型间交叉反应 [10.1128/spectrum.00040-26]。
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 成人登革热比例上升、气候适宜区扩展以及疫苗中和应答不平衡共同提示监测需突破儿童重点并强化血清分型;Qdenga数据显示仅8%的初次接种者在四价中和应答上达到平衡,DENV-4中和持续偏低 [10.1084/jem.20261126]。
literature.caveats_zh: 个别研究为预印本、回顾性病例报告或仅基于抽象信息;微流控与RT-LAMP诊断在低载量样本与生产规模化方面仍需现场验证。
literature.headline_en: Wolbachia mosquitoes and microfluidic diagnostics lead this week's dengue research highlights.
literature.lead_en: Recent dengue literature spans vector biocontrol, forecasting models, clinical biomarkers, vaccine immunology, and rapid diagnostics. A meta-analysis shows full-area Wolbachia deployments cut incidence by roughly 85%, while microfluidic and RT-LAMP tools continue to evolve for resource-limited, point-of-care serotyping.
key_findings_en: Full-area Wolbachia mosquito releases were associated with a pooled incidence rate ratio of 0.15 (95% CI 0.05–0.39), an estimated 85% reduction in dengue incidence, outperforming partial-area deployments [10.1093/trstmh/trag063].

Under a leakage-safe temporal design, an LSTM forecasting model achieved the strongest 2025 out-of-time holdout performance (MAE 7.951, R2 0.698), exceeding classical baselines in Marikina City [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10307931/v1].

Thailand surveillance (2005–2024) shows the share of adult cases aged ≥25 years nearly doubled from 19.56% to 36.16%, with Kitagawa decomposition attributing +178.7% of the shift to epidemiological rather than demographic factors [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014697].

Year-round surveillance in Tangerang, Indonesia identified DENV-2 as the dominant serotype (32.8%) and found secondary infection strongly associated with severe disease (adjusted OR 10.25, 95% CI 1.71–197.90) [10.7883/yoken.jjid.2025.232].

A dual-readout serotype-specific RT-LAMP assay detected DENV-1/2/3 in Sri Lankan clinical samples at 91.2%, 78.6%, and 100% respectively, with no cross-reactivity between serotypes [10.1128/spectrum.00040-26].
literature.trend_or_risk_en: Rising adult case proportions, expanding climatic suitability, and imbalanced vaccine neutralization collectively signal a need to broaden surveillance beyond pediatric cohorts and strengthen genomic tracking; Qdenga data show only 8% of DENV-naïve vaccinees achieving balanced tetravalent responses, with persistently poor DENV-4 neutralization [10.1084/jem.20261126].
literature.caveats_en: Several included studies are preprints, retrospective case reports, or rely on abstract-level evidence; microfluidic and RT-LAMP diagnostics still require field validation for low-titer samples and scalable manufacturing.
literature.brief_en: This week's dengue literature spans vector control, forecasting, clinical biomarkers, vaccine responses, and diagnostics. A meta-analysis of nine studies (>8 million individuals) found full-area Wolbachia mosquito releases cut dengue incidence by an estimated 85% (IRR 0.15, 95% CI 0.05–0.39). In Marikina City, an LSTM model delivered the most accurate two-week forecasts under leakage-safe evaluation. Thai surveillance revealed a near-doubling of adult cases (19.56% to 36.16%), driven primarily by epidemiological rather than demographic shifts. Indonesian surveillance documented DENV-2 dominance and a strong link between secondary infection and severe disease. Meanwhile, dual-readout RT-LAMP achieved 91–100% clinical detection across serotypes without cross-reactivity, while Qdenga immunogenicity data highlighted persistent gaps in balanced tetravalent immunity, particularly for DENV-4.

literature.zh: 本周多篇登革热研究覆盖媒介生物防控、预测模型、临床生物标志物、疫苗免疫学及快速诊断技术。一项荟萃分析显示全区域释放Wolbachia蚊可使发病率下降约85%;微流控与RT-LAMP等快速检测工具持续优化,以支持资源有限地区的现场分型需求。；Wolbachia蚊全区域释放与登革热发病率显著下降相关,合并IRR为0.15(95%CI 0.05–0.39),对应估计下降85% [10.1093/trstmh/trag063]。；在泄漏安全的时间序列设计中,基于监测数据的LSTM模型在2025年外部时间验证中表现最佳,MAE为7.951,R2为0.698 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10307931/v1]。；泰国2005–2024年监测显示25岁以上成人病例占比从19.56%升至36.16%,Kitagawa分解提示主要驱动力为流行病学因素而非人口老龄化 [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014697]。；印度尼西亚坦格朗县全年监测中DENV-2占比32.8%,继发感染与重症显著相关(调整后OR=10.25,95%CI 1.71–197.90) [10.7883/yoken.jjid.2025.232]。

Year-round surveillance in Tangerang, Indonesia identified DENV-2 as the dominant serotype (32.8%) and found secondary infection strongly associated with severe disease (adjusted OR 10.25, 95% CI 1.71–197.90) [10.7883/yoken.jjid.2025.232].

key_findings_en: Pinellas County has increased mosquito control efforts to limit the spread of Dengue Fever. This action was reported by the Pinellas County government as part of their public health initiatives. [news-ee852165561b8592]

An experimental monoclonal antibody (Dengue-mAb) was tested in a phase 2 clinical trial for its therapeutic effect against dengue virus, showing rapid clearance of viremia and fever within 24 hours at all dose levels compared to placebo. The study also noted that no causally related serious adverse events were recorded. [news-dbc3811ed7533a9d]
A locally-acquired case of dengue fever has been confirmed in Orange County, and more than 40 cases across Florida. Health officials reported the confirmation. [news-9e35db79b33ea660]

A study found that dengue patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) or oral anticoagulant therapy (OAC) had higher rates of major bleeding within 7 and 30 days of diagnosis compared to those not receiving antithrombotic therapy (ATT). The findings were reported by researchers led by Po-Tseng Lee. [news-a3177aac1a1fb98a]
Media report summarizing dengue activity across the Americas and advising travelers to monitor symptoms; status reported as preliminary and under investigation. [news-0f2cd3b0d77e4392]

papers.title: Impact of Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti on dengue incidence in endemic regions: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Dengue remains a major public health challenge in endemic regions, and conventional vector-control strategies have shown limited long-term effectiveness. The release of Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes has emerged as a novel biocontrol strategy to reduce dengue transmission. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of Wolbachia deployments in reducing dengue incidence. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library until 30 April 2025 for randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies conducted in dengue-endemic settings. Population-level effectiveness was assessed using pooled incidence rate ratios (IRRs), and individual-level protective efficacy using pooled odds ratios (ORs). Random-effects meta-analysis with restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp adjustment was applied. Subgroup analyses examined geographic region and deployment coverage. Nine studies involving >8 million individuals were included. Wolbachia deployment was associated with a substantial reduction in dengue incidence (pooled IRR 0.15, 95% CI 0.05-0.39), corresponding to an estimated 85% reduction. Full-area deployments demonstrated greater reductions (IRR 0.046, 95% CI 0.038-0.055) than partial-area deployments (IRR 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.74). Exploratory individual-level analyses yielded a pooled OR of 0.29 (95% CI 0.01-8.41) with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 86.5%).
papers.journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the effectiveness of Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti deployments in reducing dengue incidence across endemic regions. Using pooled incidence rate ratios from nine studies (>8 million individuals), the intervention demonstrated a substantial reduction in dengue incidence (pooled IRR 0.15, 85% reduction), with full-area deployments outperforming partial deployments. However, individual-level protective efficacy estimates were uncertain due to high heterogeneity (I2 = 86.5%). The findings underscore the potential of Wolbachia deployments as a dengue control strategy while emphasizing the need for further research to clarify individual-level benefits and optimize implementation strategies.

papers.title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) on Dengue Fever in Burkina Faso: Findings from the national household survey in Burkina Faso.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Dengue fever is an emerging public health concern in Burkina Faso, with increasing outbreaks and data gaps in population awareness. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to dengue fever in all health regions of the country. Methodology/Principal Findings A nationwide cross-sectional household survey was conducted in May 2022 using a stratified two-stage cluster sampling design. One rural and one urban area were selected per region. Heads of households or their representatives were interviewed using a structured questionnaire. Data were collected electronically and analyzed using Stata. A total of 1,568 participants were enrolled (52.0% male; 48.0% female). Overall, 66.3% had heard of dengue, with higher awareness in urban than rural areas. Only 49.0% correctly identified mosquito bites as the mode of transmission, and 29.9% did not know what dengue is. Most respondents (88.3%) stated that dengue can affect everyone. Regarding prevention, 80.2% reported sleeping under a mosquito net, 49.0% eliminated stagnant water, and 45.4% used mosquito repellents. In practice, 67.6% consistently slept under mosquito nets and 82.6% used repellents. Almost all respondents (98.6%) reported that they would consult a health professional if they had symptoms of dengue. However, knowledge about treatment and vaccination was limited, with 46.5% and 56.6% respectively reporting not knowing whether drugs or vaccines exist. Conclusions/Significance This study highlights moderate awareness but substantial knowledge gaps and urban–rural disparities in dengue-related KAP in Burkina Faso. Strengthening community-based education and integrated vector control strategies is essential to improve prevention and reduce dengue transmission. Author Summary Dengue fever is a mosquito-borne disease that is spreading in many parts of the world, including West Africa. In Burkina Faso, outbreaks have been reported in recent years, but little is known about what communities understand about the disease or how they protect themselves. In this study, we conducted a nationwide household survey covering all health regions of the country to explore people’s knowledge, perceptions, and prevention practices related to dengue. We found that while many people had heard about dengue, important gaps remain. A significant proportion did not know how the disease is transmitted or whether treatments or vaccines exist. Preventive actions such as sleeping under mosquito nets and removing standing water were reported, but these practices were not consistent everywhere, especially between urban and rural areas. Encouragingly, almost all respondents said they would seek care from a health professional if they developed symptoms. Our work provides the first national picture of community awareness and behaviors related to dengue in Burkina Faso. These findings highlight the need for strengthened health education and community engagement to improve prevention and support ongoing efforts to control mosquito-borne diseases.

papers.title_zh: 布基纳法索 登革热 的知识、态度和实践 (KAP):布基纳法索全国家庭调查的结果。
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Dengue fever is an emerging public health concern in Burkina Faso, with increasing outbreaks and data gaps in population awareness. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to dengue fever in all health regions of the country. Methodology/Principal Findings A nationwide cross-sectional household survey was conducted in May 2022 using a stratified two-stage cluster sampling design. One rural and one urban area were selected per region. Heads of households or their representatives were interviewed using a structured questionnaire. Data were collected electronically and analyzed using Stata. A total of 1,568 participants were enrolled (52.0% male; 48.0% female). Overall, 66.3% had heard of dengue, with higher awareness in urban than rural areas. Only 49.0% correctly identified mosquito bites as the mode of transmission, and 29.9% did not know what dengue is. Most respondents (88.3%) stated that dengue can affect everyone. Regarding prevention, 80.2% reported sleeping under a mosquito net, 49.0% eliminated stagnant water, and 45.4% used mosquito repellents. In practice, 67.6% consistently slept under mosquito nets and 82.6% used repellents. Almost all respondents (98.6%) reported that they would consult a health professional if they had symptoms of dengue. However, knowledge about treatment and vaccination was limited, with 46.5% and 56.6% respectively reporting not knowing whether drugs or vaccines exist. Conclusions/Significance This study highlights moderate awareness but substantial knowledge gaps and urban–rural disparities in dengue-related KAP in Burkina Faso. Strengthening community-based education and integrated vector control strategies is essential to improve prevention and reduce dengue transmission. Author Summary Dengue fever is a mosquito-borne disease that is spreading in many parts of the world, including West Africa. In Burkina Faso, outbreaks have been reported in recent years, but little is known about what communities understand about the disease or how they protect themselves. In this study, we conducted a nationwide household survey covering all health regions of the country to explore people’s knowledge, perceptions, and prevention practices related to dengue. We found that while many people had heard about dengue, important gaps remain. A significant proportion did not know how the disease is transmitted or whether treatments or vaccines exist. Preventive actions such as sleeping under mosquito nets and removing standing water were reported, but these practices were not consistent everywhere, especially between urban and rural areas. Encouragingly, almost all respondents said they would seek care from a health professional if they developed symptoms. Our work provides the first national picture of community awareness and behaviors related to dengue in Burkina Faso. These findings highlight the need for strengthened health education and community engagement to improve prevention and support ongoing efforts to control mosquito-borne diseases.

papers.title: Integrating Microfluidics Chips into Vector-Borne Disease Surveillance: Technological Breakthroughs and Persistent Hurdles.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vector-borne diseases (VBDs), such as malaria, dengue, and Zika virus infections, remain a critical global health burden, particularly in resource-limited regions. Conventional diagnostic methods, including microscopy, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays, and polymerase chain reaction, face significant limitations due to their reliance on centralized laboratories, lengthy processing times, and high operational costs, hindering timely disease management in remote or underserved areas. OBJECTIVE: Microfluidic diagnostics have emerged as a transformative solution, offering portability, system integration, and high sensitivity through miniaturized fluidic control and multiplexed detection capabilities. These devices enable rapid, on-site diagnosis by combining sample preparation, target amplification, and signal readout into a single chip, aligning with the growing demand for point-of-care testing. METHODS: This review was conducted following a systematic literature search of PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus databases from January 2010 to June 2026. Search terms included combinations of "microfluidic," "lab-on-a-chip," "point-of-care," "vector-borne disease," "malaria," "dengue," "Zika," "West Nile virus," "Lyme disease," and "CRISPR." Inclusion criteria were (1) peer-reviewed articles reporting microfluidic chip applications for VBD pathogen detection or vector surveillance; (2) studies describing field-deployable or clinically validated platforms; and (3) publications in English. Exclusion criteria included purely theoretical modeling studies without experimental validation and nonchip-based microfluidic systems. A total of 87 studies were selected for qualitative synthesis after title/abstract screening and full-text evaluation. We critically evaluate real-world application scenarios, including field deployments for malaria surveillance in Uganda and outbreak responses to arboviral infections in Brazil and Southeast Asia, while addressing persistent translational barriers such as manufacturing standardization, sample pretreatment complexity, and cost-effectiveness. RESULTS: Key findings demonstrate the successful integration of sample-to-answer workflows on miniaturized platforms, achieving significant reductions in detection time and operational dependencies compared with conventional laboratory methods. Critical challenges identified include manufacturing scalability for resource-limited settings, complex sample pretreatment requirements, and the pressing need for cost reduction to ensure sustainable deployment in endemic regions. CONCLUSION: This review aims to explore emerging integration strategies beyond conventional diagnostics, focusing on approaches such as CRISPR-based assays, artificial intelligence-driven image analysis, and scalable manufacturing processes to strengthen global VBD control networks and improve clinical outcomes in underserved populations. CONCLUSION: This review aims to explore emerging integration strategies beyond conventional diagnostics, focusing on approaches such as CRISPR-based assays, simplified image analysis, and scalable manufacturing processes to strengthen global VBD control networks and improve clinical outcomes in underserved populations. Specific recommendations for phased deployment in endemic regions, including pilot beta-testing programs and technology transfer partnerships, are proposed to accelerate translational impact.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Vector-borne diseases such as dengue impose a substantial global health burden, particularly in resource-limited settings where conventional diagnostics face critical limitations in timeliness, portability, and cost. The study highlights the need for innovative diagnostic approaches to overcome these barriers and enable effective disease management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This systematic review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature on microfluidic chip applications for vector-borne disease pathogen detection and vector surveillance published between January 2010 and June 2026. Included studies reported field-deployable or clinically validated microfluidic platforms for detecting pathogens including dengue virus.
analysis.methods: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus using targeted terms related to microfluidics, point-of-care testing, and vector-borne diseases. Inclusion criteria required experimental validation of microfluidic chip-based detection platforms, while exclusion criteria removed purely theoretical modeling studies and non-chip-based microfluidic systems.
analysis.main_results: The review identified 87 studies demonstrating successful integration of sample-to-answer workflows on miniaturized microfluidic platforms for vector-borne disease detection, achieving significant reductions in detection time and operational dependencies compared with conventional laboratory methods.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that microfluidic diagnostics can transform point-of-care testing for vector-borne diseases by enabling rapid, on-site diagnosis through integrated sample preparation, amplification, and detection. The novelty lies in synthesizing real-world application scenarios and identifying translational barriers specific to field deployment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the potential of microfluidic diagnostics to strengthen surveillance and clinical management of dengue and other arboviral infections in endemic regions by reducing diagnostic delays and operational costs. The review proposes phased deployment strategies and technology transfer partnerships to accelerate practical implementation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence base is limited by the absence of quantitative performance metrics for dengue-specific platforms and reliance on qualitative synthesis of heterogeneous studies. The strength of evidence is moderate due to identified translational barriers including manufacturing scalability, sample pretreatment complexity, and cost-effectiveness concerns.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the role of microfluidic diagnostics in addressing persistent challenges of conventional vector-borne disease diagnostics, with a focus on dengue virus detection. The authors synthesize evidence from 87 studies published between 2010 and 2026, highlighting successful integration of sample-to-answer workflows on miniaturized platforms that reduce detection time and operational dependencies compared to traditional laboratory methods. While the review demonstrates the potential of microfluidic chips to enable rapid, on-site diagnosis through integrated sample preparation and detection, it identifies critical translational barriers including manufacturing scalability, complex sample pretreatment requirements, and cost constraints that limit sustainable deployment in endemic regions. The authors propose phased deployment strategies and technology transfer partnerships to accelerate practical implementation of these technologies for strengthening dengue surveillance and clinical management in resource-limited settings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热等 媒介 传播疾病给全球带来了巨大的健康负担,特别是在资源有限的环境中,传统诊断在及时性、便携性和成本方面面临严重限制。该研究强调需要创新的诊断方法来克服这些障碍并实现有效的疾病管理。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本系统综述综合了 2010 年 1 月至 2026 年 6 月发表的有关 媒介 传播疾病病原体检测的微流控芯片应用和 媒介 监测 的同行评审文献。纳入的研究报告了用于检测病原体(包括 登革病毒)的可现场部署或临床验证的微流控平台。
elements_zh.methods: 使用与微流体、即时检测和 Z​​XQTERMAEQXZ 传播疾病相关的目标术语在 PubMed、Web of Science 和 Scopus 中进行了系统的文献检索。纳入标准需要对基于微流控芯片的检测平台进行实验验证,而排除标准则删除了纯粹的理论建模研究和非基于芯片的微流控系统。
elements_zh.main_results: 该审查确定了 87 项研究,这些研究证明了在小型化微流体平台上成功集成了样本到答案工作流程,用于 媒介 传播的疾病检测,与传统实验室方法相比,显着减少了检测时间和操作依赖性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明微流体诊断可以通过集成的样品制备、扩增和检测实现快速现场 诊断,从而改变 媒介 传播疾病的现场检测。新颖之处在于综合现实世界的应用场景并识别特定于现场部署的转化障碍。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持微流体诊断通过减少诊断延迟和运营成本来加强流行地区登革热和其他虫媒病毒感染的 监测 和临床管理的潜力。审查提出了分阶段部署战略和技术转让伙伴关系,以加速实际实施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于缺乏针对登革热特定平台的定量性能指标以及依赖于异质性研究的定性综合,证据基础受到限制。由于已确定的转化障碍(包括制造可扩展性、样品预处理复杂性和成本效益问题),证据的强度是中等的。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热等 媒介 传播疾病给全球带来了巨大的健康负担,特别是在资源有限的环境中,传统诊断在及时性、便携性和成本方面面临严重限制。该研究强调需要创新的诊断方法来克服这些障碍并实现有效的疾病管理。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本系统综述综合了 2010 年 1 月至 2026 年 6 月发表的有关 媒介 传播疾病病原体检测的微流控芯片应用和 媒介 监测 的同行评审文献。纳入的研究报告了用于检测病原体(包括 登革病毒)的可现场部署或临床验证的微流控平台。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用与微流体、即时检测和 Z​​XQTERMAEQXZ 传播疾病相关的目标术语在 PubMed、Web of Science 和 Scopus 中进行了系统的文献检索。纳入标准需要对基于微流控芯片的检测平台进行实验验证,而排除标准则删除了纯粹的理论建模研究和非基于芯片的微流控系统。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该审查确定了 87 项研究,这些研究证明了在小型化微流体平台上成功集成了样本到答案工作流程,用于 媒介 传播的疾病检测,与传统实验室方法相比,显着减少了检测时间和操作依赖性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明微流体诊断可以通过集成的样品制备、扩增和检测实现快速现场 诊断,从而改变 媒介 传播疾病的现场检测。新颖之处在于综合现实世界的应用场景并识别特定于现场部署的转化障碍。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持微流体诊断通过减少诊断延迟和运营成本来加强流行地区登革热和其他虫媒病毒感染的 监测 和临床管理的潜力。审查提出了分阶段部署战略和技术转让伙伴关系,以加速实际实施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于缺乏针对登革热特定平台的定量性能指标以及依赖于异质性研究的定性综合,证据基础受到限制。由于已确定的转化障碍(包括制造可扩展性、样品预处理复杂性和成本效益问题),证据的强度是中等的。

papers.title: Year-Round Dengue Surveillance in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia (2024): Clinical and Virological Features with Biomarker Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Dengue remains a major public health concern in Indonesia. This study aimed to describe the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, immune responses, and genotype characterization of dengue virus (DENV) infections in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia. A year-round prospective surveillance was conducted from January 2024-January 2025 at a district hospital and two primary health centers. Febrile patients aged ≥4 years were tested using dengue NS1, IgM/IgG rapid tests, ELISA, and RT-PCR, and serum biomarkers (angiopoietin-2, IL-6, ferritin, sCD163) were quantified. Of 404 participants, 240 (59.4%) had confirmed dengue. Among RT-PCR-serotyped cases (n=192), the distribution was DENV-2 63/192 (32.8%), DENV-1 60/192 (31.3%), DENV-3 47/192 (24.5%), and DENV-4 22/192 (11.5%). Among hospitalized dengue cases (n=144), secondary infection (131/144, 91.0%) was associated with severe disease (adjusted OR=10.25; 95% CI: 1.71-197.90, p=0.034). Biomarker levels were elevated in dengue cases but did not discriminate severity, indicating the need for validation in larger cohorts using standardized definitions. Sequencing identified DENV-1 genotypes I and IV, DENV-2 Cosmopolitan, DENV-3 genotype I, and DENV-4 genotype IIa; one DENV-4 isolate carried an EDIII E384 D→H substitution warranting further investigation. Continued genomic surveillance and vaccine development that induces balanced, serotype-specific immunity are needed to support national and global dengue control.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted year-round dengue surveillance in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia, from January 2024 to January 2025, focusing on the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, immune responses, and genotype distribution of dengue virus (DENV) infections. However, the study's reliance on a limited number of healthcare facilities may affect its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

analysis_zh.methods: 使用登革热NS1、IgM/IgG快速检测、ELISA和RT-PCR对年龄≥4岁的发热患者进行检测,并对血清生物标志物(血管生成素-2、IL-6、铁蛋白、sCD163)进行定量。测序鉴定出DENV-1基因型I和IV、DENV-2 Cosmopolitan、DENV-3基因型I和DENV-4基因型IIa;一种 DENV-4 分离株携带 EDIII E384 D→H 取代,值得进一步研究。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究深入了解了 登革病毒 感染的血清型分布和临床特征,强调了继发感染与严重疾病之间的关联。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 监测 策略提供信息,并强调开发 疫苗 的必要性,以诱导平衡的血清型特异性免疫来支持登革热控制。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖单一地区医院和初级卫生中心而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。由于观察设计和潜在的混杂因素,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: CORRELATION BETWEEN NEUTROPHIL LYMPHOCYTE RATIO, PLATELET LYMPHOCYTE RATIO AND DENGUE FEVER IN CHILDREN-A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY.
papers.abstract: Dengue is a re-emerging tropical disease transmitted by mosquitoes. This cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Paediatrics of a tertiary care centre in South India over two years. Children and adolescents aged 0-15 years who presented with fever and were confirmed to have dengue by serological tests were included in this study. Blood was collected and sent for complete blood count (CBC) on day 3 of illness. Neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were derived. The sensitivity of NLR and PLR was 68.4% and 96.8% respectively, while the specificity of NLR and PLR were 41.7% and 66.7% respectively. Although PLR was found to have higher sensitivity and specificity, NLR was found to have an increased positive predictive value. The platelet-lymphocyte ratio demonstrates superiority by overall accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity, proving to be a more effective marker for identifying severe dengue cases. NLR and PLR demonstrated a strong positive correlation (r = 0.83, p <0.001). The clinical utility of these ratios has been extensively studied in other diseases, such as sepsis and COVID-19, especially in adults, but has been underutilized in children due to the lack of knowledge and limited research.

The research was motivated by the need to identify effective biomarkers for early detection of dengue in children.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted over two years in the Department of Paediatrics at a tertiary care centre in South India. Children and adolescents aged 0-15 years who presented with fever and were confirmed to have dengue by serological tests were included in the study.
analysis.methods: Blood samples were collected and analyzed for complete blood count (CBC) on day 3 of illness. NLR and PLR were calculated from the CBC results. The study used these ratios to assess their potential as biomarkers for dengue fever in children.
analysis.main_results: NLR and PLR demonstrated a strong positive correlation (r = 0.83, p < 0.001). The sensitivity of NLR and PLR was 68.4% and 96.8% respectively, while the specificity of NLR and PLR were 41.7% and 66.7% respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that although PLR had higher sensitivity and specificity, NLR showed an increased positive predictive value. This suggests that NLR may be more useful in identifying severe dengue cases in children.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of more effective biomarkers for early detection and risk assessment of severe dengue in children, potentially improving clinical decision-making and public health surveillance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on serological confirmation and the lack of longitudinal data.

The results showed a strong positive correlation between NLR and PLR (r = 0.83, p < 0.001). While PLR had higher sensitivity and specificity, NLR demonstrated an increased positive predictive value. The study suggests that NLR may be more effective in identifying severe dengue cases in children. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on serological confirmation and the absence of longitudinal data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨儿童中性粒细胞-淋巴细胞比值(NLR)和血小板-淋巴细胞比值(PLR)与登革热之间的相关性,因为这些比值已在其他疾病中进行了研究,但在儿科登革热病例中的研究还不够充分。这项研究的动机是需要确定有效的生物标志物以早期检测儿童登革热。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 印度南部一家三级护理中心的儿科进行了一项为期两年的横断面研究。该研究纳入了出现发烧症状并经血清学检测证实患有登革热的0-15岁儿童和青少年。
elements_zh.methods: 在患病第 3 天收集血样并进行全血细胞计数 (CBC) 分析。NLR 和 PLR 根据 CBC 结果计算。该研究使用这些比率来评估它们作为儿童 登革热 生物标志物的潜力。
elements_zh.main_results: NLR 和 PLR 显示出很强的正相关性(r = 0.83,p < 0.001)。NLR和PLR的敏感性分别为68.4%和96.8%,NLR和PLR的特异性分别为41.7%和66.7%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,虽然PLR具有更高的敏感性和特异性,但NLR表现出更高的阳性预测价值。这表明 NLR 在识别儿童 重症登革热 病例方面可能更有用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发更有效的生物标志物,用于儿童 重症登革热 的早期检测和风险评估,从而有可能改善临床决策和公共卫生 监测。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,无法确定因果关系。由于依赖血清学确认且缺乏纵向数据,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 儿童中性粒细胞淋巴细胞比率、血小板淋巴细胞比率和 登革热 之间的相关性 - 横断面研究。
papers.source_body_en: Dengue is a re-emerging tropical disease transmitted by mosquitoes. papers.abstract_zh: 登革热是一种重新出现的由蚊子传播的热带疾病。这项横断面研究是在印度南部一家三级护理中心的儿科进行的,历时两年多。本研究纳入了出现发烧症状并经血清学检测证实患有登革热的0-15岁儿童和青少年。在患病第 3 天采集血液并送去进行全血细胞计数 (CBC)。得出中性粒细胞-淋巴细胞比率(NLR)和血小板-淋巴细胞比率(PLR)。NLR和PLR的敏感性分别为68.4%和96.8%,NLR和PLR的特异性分别为41.7%和66.7%。尽管发现 PLR 具有更高的敏感性和特异性,但发现 NLR 具有更高的阳性预测价值。血小板-淋巴细胞比率在总体准确性、特异性和敏感性方面表现出优越性,被证明是识别 重症登革热 病例的更有效标记。NLR 和 PLR 显示出很强的正相关性(r = 0.83,p <0.001)。这些比率的临床效用已在脓毒症和 COVID-19 等其他疾病中得到了广泛研究,尤其是在成人中,但由于缺乏知识和研究有限,在儿童中尚未得到充分利用。

papers.title: Evaluation of inactivated and live attenuated, tetravalent dengue vaccine prime-boost strategies in a randomized, open-label, phase I study: implications for understanding immune correlates of protection.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Vaccines that elicit balanced, protective immunity to all four dengue virus (DENV) types are needed to reduce the global burden of dengue disease. Achieving this goal has been a challenge for dengue vaccine developers, particularly when immunizing dengue immunologically naïve individuals. In this randomized, phase I, open-label study of 40 healthy adults, we evaluated a heterologous, tetravalent purified inactivated vaccine (PIV) prime and a tetravalent live attenuated vaccine (LAV) boost. We compared a 0, 90 day PIV/LAV prime-boost schedule to a 0, 180 day schedule. These two PIV/LAV regimens elicited similar, high, and balanced cellular and humoral immune responses to DENV 1-4, although the condensed schedule was associated with more severe adverse events. In a subsequent clinical trial [K. Friberg, et al., Lancet Infect Dis 24:896-908, 2024, https://doi.org/10.1016/S1473-3099(24)00100-2], the PIV/LAV vaccinees were challenged with DENV-1 and most were unprotected and experienced more pronounced dengue fever-like illness than unvaccinated controls. These outcomes underscore critical gaps in our understanding of mechanistic correlates of dengue vaccine-mediated protection and disease risk. IMPORTANCE: Dengue vaccine research and development has been complicated by several factors, including an incomplete understanding of immunologic correlates of protection and immune-mediated risk of severe disease. High and balanced immunity elicited by the tetravalent purified inactivated vaccine (PIV)/live attenuated vaccine (LAV) prime-boost vaccine strategy was predicted to provide protection from dengue virus type 1 (DENV-1) challenge in a subsequent clinical study, but vaccinees were unprotected and had an unexpected increase in symptom severity compared to unvaccinated controls. Evidence of exposure to a specific DENV type by viral genome detection (e.g., by quantitative RT-PCR) in acute samples or measurement of post-exposure, type-specific antibody responses (e.g., by serum antibody depletion) are known correlates of protection. However, current methods of measuring type-specific antibody are not ideal for evaluating groups of vaccinees, even in relatively small clinical trials. Newer, high-throughput methods of determining DENV type-specific immune responses and discovery of other correlates of protection are needed to more reliably evaluate dengue vaccine candidates.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated two prime-boost vaccination strategies for a tetravalent dengue vaccine in 40 healthy adults. The researchers compared a 0, 90 day schedule of purified inactivated vaccine (PIV) and live attenuated vaccine (LAV) with a 0, 180 day schedule. Both regimens elicited high and balanced immune responses, but the shorter schedule was linked to more severe adverse events. In a follow-up trial, vaccinated individuals were unprotected and experienced more severe dengue-like symptoms compared to unvaccinated controls. These results highlight the need for better understanding of immune correlates of protection and improved methods for evaluating vaccine efficacy. The study's findings have implications for vaccine development and the design of future trials, but the evidence is limited by the small sample size and the challenges in measuring immune responses accurately.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 需要针对所有四种 登革病毒 (DENV) 类型的登革热 疫苗 产生平衡免疫力,以减轻登革热疾病的全球负担。实现这一目标对于登革热 疫苗 开发人员来说是一个挑战,特别是在对登革热免疫学上未接触过的个体进行免疫接种时。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: This study was a randomized, phase I, open-label trial involving 40 healthy adults. The study evaluated a heterologous, tetravalent purified inactivated vaccine (PIV) prime and a tetravalent live attenuated vaccine (LAV) boost regimen. The researchers compared two schedules: 0, 90 day and 0, 180 day.
elements_zh.methods: 该研究通过定量 RT-PCR 在急性样本中使用病毒 基因组 检测,并使用血清抗体消耗测量暴露后的类型特异性抗体反应。这些方法是已知的保护相关方法。然而,目前测量类型特异性抗体的方法对于在小型临床试验中评估 疫苗 并不理想。
elements_zh.main_results: 两种 PIV/LAV 方案引发与 DENV 1-4 类似、高且平衡的细胞和体液 免疫应答。然而,浓缩的 0 天、90 天时间表与更严重的不良事件相关。在随后的临床试验中,与未接种疫苗的对照组相比,疫苗 没有受到保护,并且经历了更明显的 登革热 样疾病。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果凸显了在理解登革热 疫苗 介导的保护和疾病风险的机制相关性方面的关键差距。该研究强调需要改进方法来评估 免疫应答 并确定保护的相关性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究结果强调了了解保护的免疫相关性以及与不同 疫苗接种 方案相关的潜在风险的重要性,为开发更有效的登革热 疫苗 提供了信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的样本量较小以及对特定 免疫应答 测量的依赖可能会限制普遍性。证据是中等的,因为结果是基于单次试验和随后的临床挑战,所使用的测量技术存在一些局限性。

papers.title_zh: 在随机、开放标签、I 期研究中评估灭活和减毒活四价登革热 疫苗 初免加强策略:对了解保护的免疫相关性的影响。
papers.source_body_en: UNLABELLED: Vaccines that elicit balanced, protective immunity to all four dengue virus (DENV) types are needed to reduce the global burden of dengue disease. Achieving this goal has been a challenge for dengue vaccine developers, particularly when immunizing dengue immunologically naïve individuals. In this randomized, phase I, open-label study of 40 healthy adults, we evaluated a heterologous, tetravalent purified inactivated vaccine (PIV) prime and a tetravalent live attenuated vaccine (LAV) boost. We compared a 0, 90 day PIV/LAV prime-boost schedule to a 0, 180 day schedule. These two PIV/LAV regimens elicited similar, high, and balanced cellular and humoral immune responses to DENV 1-4, although the condensed schedule was associated with more severe adverse events. In a subsequent clinical trial [K. Friberg, et al., Lancet Infect Dis 24:896-908, 2024, https://doi.org/10.1016/S1473-3099(24)00100-2], the PIV/LAV vaccinees were challenged with DENV-1 and most were unprotected and experienced more pronounced dengue fever-like illness than unvaccinated controls. These outcomes underscore critical gaps in our understanding of mechanistic correlates of dengue vaccine-mediated protection and disease risk. IMPORTANCE: Dengue vaccine research and development has been complicated by several factors, including an incomplete understanding of immunologic correlates of protection and immune-mediated risk of severe disease. High and balanced immunity elicited by the tetravalent purified inactivated vaccine (PIV)/live attenuated vaccine (LAV) prime-boost vaccine strategy was predicted to provide protection from dengue virus type 1 (DENV-1) challenge in a subsequent clinical study, but vaccinees were unprotected and had an unexpected increase in symptom severity compared to unvaccinated controls. Evidence of exposure to a specific DENV type by viral genome detection (e.g., by quantitative RT-PCR) in acute samples or measurement of post-exposure, type-specific antibody responses (e.g., by serum antibody depletion) are known correlates of protection. However, current methods of measuring type-specific antibody are not ideal for evaluating groups of vaccinees, even in relatively small clinical trials. Newer, high-throughput methods of determining DENV type-specific immune responses and discovery of other correlates of protection are needed to more reliably evaluate dengue vaccine candidates.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 需要针对所有四种 登革病毒 (DENV) 类型的登革热 疫苗 产生平衡免疫力,以减轻登革热疾病的全球负担。实现这一目标对于登革热 疫苗 开发人员来说是一个挑战,特别是在对登革热免疫学上未接触过的个体进行免疫接种时。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究通过定量 RT-PCR 在急性样本中使用病毒 基因组 检测,并使用血清抗体消耗测量暴露后的类型特异性抗体反应。这些方法是已知的保护相关方法。然而,目前测量类型特异性抗体的方法对于在小型临床试验中评估 疫苗 并不理想。
analysis_zh.main_results: 两种 PIV/LAV 方案引发与 DENV 1-4 类似、高且平衡的细胞和体液 免疫应答。然而,浓缩的 0 天、90 天时间表与更严重的不良事件相关。在随后的临床试验中,与未接种疫苗的对照组相比,疫苗 没有受到保护,并且经历了更明显的 登革热 样疾病。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果凸显了在理解登革热 疫苗 介导的保护和疾病风险的机制相关性方面的关键差距。该研究强调需要改进方法来评估 免疫应答 并确定保护的相关性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究结果强调了了解保护的免疫相关性以及与不同 疫苗接种 方案相关的潜在风险的重要性,为开发更有效的登革热 疫苗 提供了信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的样本量较小以及对特定 免疫应答 测量的依赖可能会限制普遍性。证据是中等的,因为结果是基于单次试验和随后的临床挑战,所使用的测量技术存在一些局限性。

papers.title: The spatial structure of dengue transmission in Kamphaeng Phet Thailand.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito transmitted arbovirus that represents a severe threat to global populations. The four serotypes of DENV often circulate endemically resulting in many discrete but overlapping transmission chains in space and time, effectively hiding the underlying patterns of transmission, and longer term consequences on local population immunity. Here we combined serotyped case data with sequence data from a single setting over 25 years to characterise the spatial dependence between cases, the number of distinct transmission chains circulating at any time and whether community transmission was followed by serotype-specific local herd immunity. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: In this study, we combined geolocated case data (N = 7,487) from individuals that presented at a provincial hospital in Kamphaeng Phet Province, Thailand alongside a subset of the sequences of the viruses (N = 302) that infected them. We estimated the spatial dependence between case pairs over different temporal and spatial windows, using both serotype and sequence data, and used logistic regression to identify whether host population size or epidemic size were correlated with viral diversity. We found there was spatial dependence between cases at up to 5 km, resulting in localised serotype-specific patterns of immunity in subsequent years. Within a 78.5 km2 area there were 9.6 distinct transmission chains at any time and that each 100,000 increase in population size was associated with 9.8 additional chains. While local viral diversity was also correlated with the size of the epidemic within any month, we found diversity only had moderate predictive power to accurately recover epidemic dynamics. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: These findings highlight the nuanced and spatially variable ecology of a highly endemic pathogen with substantial immunity. This study also illustrates the strengths of combining multiple data sources to shed light on the nature of DENV transmission.

papers.title_zh: 泰国甘烹碧登革热 传播 的空间结构。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito transmitted arbovirus that represents a severe threat to global populations. The four serotypes of DENV often circulate endemically resulting in many discrete but overlapping transmission chains in space and time, effectively hiding the underlying patterns of transmission, and longer term consequences on local population immunity. Here we combined serotyped case data with sequence data from a single setting over 25 years to characterise the spatial dependence between cases, the number of distinct transmission chains circulating at any time and whether community transmission was followed by serotype-specific local herd immunity. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: In this study, we combined geolocated case data (N = 7,487) from individuals that presented at a provincial hospital in Kamphaeng Phet Province, Thailand alongside a subset of the sequences of the viruses (N = 302) that infected them. We estimated the spatial dependence between case pairs over different temporal and spatial windows, using both serotype and sequence data, and used logistic regression to identify whether host population size or epidemic size were correlated with viral diversity. We found there was spatial dependence between cases at up to 5 km, resulting in localised serotype-specific patterns of immunity in subsequent years. Within a 78.5 km2 area there were 9.6 distinct transmission chains at any time and that each 100,000 increase in population size was associated with 9.8 additional chains. While local viral diversity was also correlated with the size of the epidemic within any month, we found diversity only had moderate predictive power to accurately recover epidemic dynamics. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: These findings highlight the nuanced and spatially variable ecology of a highly endemic pathogen with substantial immunity. This study also illustrates the strengths of combining multiple data sources to shed light on the nature of DENV transmission.

papers.title: Epidemiological shift in age distribution of Dengue in Thailand, 2005–2024
papers.abstract: Dengue has historically been characterized as a childhood disease, but evidence of shifting age distribution is increasing. We analyzed 20 years (2005–2024) of national dengue surveillance data from Thailand comprising 1,639,442 cases to examine temporal trends in age-specific incidence, quantify age shift magnitude using the ratio of incidence rate ratios (RIRR), and decompose observed changes using Kitagawa decomposition. The proportion of cases among adults ≥25 years nearly doubled from 19.56% to 36.16%, while the children's proportion declined from 54.49% to 41.63%. RIRR for adults 25–44 years was 1.78 (95% CI 1.76-1.80), and for older adults ≥45 years was 2.19 (95% CI 2.15-2.24). Kitagawa decomposition attributed +178.7% of change to epidemiological factors and -78.7% to demographic shifts, supporting a declining force of infection rather than population aging as the primary driver. These findings necessitate expanding dengue prevention beyond school-based programs and enhancing clinical vigilance for adult dengue.

papers.title_zh: 2005-2024 年泰国登革热年龄分布的流行病学变化
papers.source_body_en: Dengue has historically been characterized as a childhood disease, but evidence of shifting age distribution is increasing. We analyzed 20 years (2005–2024) of national dengue surveillance data from Thailand comprising 1,639,442 cases to examine temporal trends in age-specific incidence, quantify age shift magnitude using the ratio of incidence rate ratios (RIRR), and decompose observed changes using Kitagawa decomposition. The proportion of cases among adults ≥25 years nearly doubled from 19.56% to 36.16%, while the children's proportion declined from 54.49% to 41.63%. RIRR for adults 25–44 years was 1.78 (95% CI 1.76-1.80), and for older adults ≥45 years was 2.19 (95% CI 2.15-2.24). Kitagawa decomposition attributed +178.7% of change to epidemiological factors and -78.7% to demographic shifts, supporting a declining force of infection rather than population aging as the primary driver. These findings necessitate expanding dengue prevention beyond school-based programs and enhancing clinical vigilance for adult dengue.

papers.title: Emerging and Re-Emerging Viral Pathogens in Oncolytic Virotherapy: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.abstract: Oncolytic virotherapy has recently emerged as a promising immuno-oncological strategy, utilising the natural cytolytic potentials of viral pathogens to selectively target and destroy malignant cells. Although various engineered viruses, such as adenoviruses, vaccinia virus, and herpes simplex virus, are currently in clinical evaluation, emerging and re-emerging viruses with intrinsic oncolytic potential, including Zika virus (ZIKV), Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Dengue virus (DENV), and West Nile virus (WNV), have also shown promising results. These emerging and re-emerging viral pathogens show specific tumour tropism, immune evasion strategies, and immunogenic cell death mechanisms that could be harnessed for next-generation therapeutic platforms. Nonetheless, concerns related to safety, viral pathogenicity, host immune responses, and the risk of uncontrolled viral dissemination present significant translational challenges. The present review provides a comprehensive overview of novel viral candidates, including ZIKV, SARS-CoV-2, DENV, and WNV, in oncolytic virotherapy, their molecular mechanisms of tumour targeting, and current advancements in genetic engineering aimed at improving therapeutic efficacy and biosafety. Moreover, this review describes clinical perspectives, regulatory considerations, and future directions in integrating emerging virotherapeutic agents into precision oncology.

papers.title: Mosquito diversity and arbovirus detection in Paraguay: first evidence of dengue and chikungunya virus infection in field populations.
papers.abstract: Arboviruses are mosquito-borne viruses of major public health importance, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. In Paraguay, dengue (DENV) and chikungunya (CHIKV) viruses are among the most epidemiologically relevant; however, studies integrating mosquito and arbovirus surveillance remain scarce. This study aimed to characterize mosquito assemblage composition across different ecological settings and investigate arbovirus circulation in field-collected mosquitoes. A total of 4,595 mosquitoes (609 pools) were collected between 2013 and 2024 from urban, rural, and Atlantic Forest environments in Paraguay. Twenty-six mosquito species were identified, with Culex quinquefasciatus (55.3%) as the most abundant, followed by Aedes (Ochlerotatus) scapularis (13.3%). Aedes aegypti (7.3%) was mainly associated with urban areas. Diversity analyses showed higher alpha diversity and greater gamma diversity in the Atlantic Forest and lower values in rural areas, whereas high beta diversity indicated substantial species turnover among locations. Molecular screening by real-time RT-PCR detected no evidence of West Nile, Saint Louis encephalitis, Venezuelan equine encephalitis, Mayaro, yellow fever, Zika, or Oropouche viruses. aegypti pools tested positive for DENV (n=3; 2021 and 2023) and CHIKV (n=3; 2023). Phylogenetic reconstruction confirmed the circulation of DENV-4 Genotype II (lineage B.1.1), DENV-2 Genotype II (F.1.1.2), and CHIKV East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineages in Paraguay, all closely related to human outbreak-associated sequences. These findings provide the first molecular evidence of arbovirus infection in field-collected mosquitoes in Paraguay and emphasize the importance of integrated entomological and viral surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arboviruses transmitted by mosquitoes pose significant public health threats in tropical and subtropical regions, yet Paraguay lacked integrated studies linking mosquito diversity with arbovirus circulation. The study addressed the knowledge gap by investigating arbovirus presence in field-collected mosquitoes across diverse ecological settings in Paraguay.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 4,595 mosquitoes (609 pools) were collected between 2013 and 2024 from urban, rural, and Atlantic Forest environments in Paraguay. Twenty-six mosquito species were identified, with Culex quinquefasciatus as the most abundant, followed by Aedes (Ochlerotatus) scapularis and Aedes aegypti.
analysis.methods: Molecular screening by real-time RT-PCR was used to detect arboviruses in mosquito pools. Phylogenetic reconstruction was performed to characterize viral lineages.
analysis.main_results: Dengue virus (DENV) was detected in three Aedes aegypti pools (2021 and 2023), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in three pools (2023). Phylogenetic analysis identified DENV-4 Genotype II (lineage B.1.1), DENV-2 Genotype II (F.1.1.2), and CHIKV East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineages, all closely related to human outbreak-associated sequences.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The detection of DENV and CHIKV in field-collected mosquitoes provides the first molecular evidence of arbovirus circulation in Paraguay, highlighting the need for integrated entomological and viral surveillance to monitor emerging and re-emerging arboviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted vector control and surveillance strategies in Paraguay, particularly in urban areas where Aedes aegypti predominates, to mitigate dengue and chikungunya transmission risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s reliance on field-collected mosquitoes and limited temporal sampling may underrepresent viral diversity and transmission dynamics, warranting broader longitudinal surveillance to strengthen evidence.

These findings represent the first molecular evidence of arbovirus infection in field-collected mosquitoes in Paraguay, emphasizing the importance of integrated entomological and viral surveillance to monitor emerging and re-emerging arboviruses.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Arboviruses transmitted by mosquitoes pose significant public health threats in tropical and subtropical regions, yet Paraguay lacked integrated studies linking mosquito diversity with arbovirus circulation. The study addressed the knowledge gap by investigating arbovirus presence in field-collected mosquitoes across diverse ecological settings in Paraguay.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A total of 4,595 mosquitoes (609 pools) were collected between 2013 and 2024 from urban, rural, and Atlantic Forest environments in Paraguay. Twenty-six mosquito species were identified, with Culex quinquefasciatus as the most abundant, followed by Aedes (Ochlerotatus) scapularis and Aedes aegypti.
analysis_en.methods: Molecular screening by real-time RT-PCR was used to detect arboviruses in mosquito pools. Phylogenetic reconstruction was performed to characterize viral lineages.
analysis_en.main_results: Dengue virus (DENV) was detected in three Aedes aegypti pools (2021 and 2023), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in three pools (2023). Phylogenetic analysis identified DENV-4 Genotype II (lineage B.1.1), DENV-2 Genotype II (F.1.1.2), and CHIKV East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineages, all closely related to human outbreak-associated sequences.

analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted vector control and surveillance strategies in Paraguay, particularly in urban areas where Aedes aegypti predominates, to mitigate dengue and chikungunya transmission risks.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s reliance on field-collected mosquitoes and limited temporal sampling may underrepresent viral diversity and transmission dynamics, warranting broader longitudinal surveillance to strengthen evidence.

papers.title_zh: 巴拉圭的蚊子多样性和虫媒病毒检测:野外人群中登革热和基孔肯雅病毒感染的第一个证据。
papers.source_body_en: Arboviruses are mosquito-borne viruses of major public health importance, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. In Paraguay, dengue (DENV) and chikungunya (CHIKV) viruses are among the most epidemiologically relevant; however, studies integrating mosquito and arbovirus surveillance remain scarce. This study aimed to characterize mosquito assemblage composition across different ecological settings and investigate arbovirus circulation in field-collected mosquitoes. A total of 4,595 mosquitoes (609 pools) were collected between 2013 and 2024 from urban, rural, and Atlantic Forest environments in Paraguay. Twenty-six mosquito species were identified, with Culex quinquefasciatus (55.3%) as the most abundant, followed by Aedes (Ochlerotatus) scapularis (13.3%). Aedes aegypti (7.3%) was mainly associated with urban areas. Diversity analyses showed higher alpha diversity and greater gamma diversity in the Atlantic Forest and lower values in rural areas, whereas high beta diversity indicated substantial species turnover among locations. Molecular screening by real-time RT-PCR detected no evidence of West Nile, Saint Louis encephalitis, Venezuelan equine encephalitis, Mayaro, yellow fever, Zika, or Oropouche viruses. aegypti pools tested positive for DENV (n=3; 2021 and 2023) and CHIKV (n=3; 2023). Phylogenetic reconstruction confirmed the circulation of DENV-4 Genotype II (lineage B.1.1), DENV-2 Genotype II (F.1.1.2), and CHIKV East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineages in Paraguay, all closely related to human outbreak-associated sequences. These findings provide the first molecular evidence of arbovirus infection in field-collected mosquitoes in Paraguay and emphasize the importance of integrated entomological and viral surveillance.

papers.title: Invasive Aspergillosis Following Dengue: An Autopsy Case and Review of the Literature.
papers.abstract: Invasive aspergillosis typically occurs in immunocompromised hosts but has been increasingly recognized following viral illnesses, including dengue and coronavirus disease 2019. Herein, a fatal case of disseminated aspergillosis following severe dengue is described, and the association is systematically reviewed. A previously healthy 25-year-old woman presented with fever and multiorgan dysfunction. Dengue IgM results were positive, and other tropical infections were excluded. Despite intensive care, the patient developed progressive respiratory failure, refractory shock, and acute kidney injury and died. An autopsy revealed diffuse alveolar damage and extensive invasive aspergillosis involving the bronchi, pulmonary vasculature, and myocardium. In the present systematic review, 21 additional cases of invasive aspergillosis following dengue (total n = 22; median age 36 years, 59% male) were identified, predominantly in Asia. Fifteen cases (68%) had pulmonary involvement. Most patients had severe dengue with multiorgan dysfunction. The overall mortality was 63.6%; 23% of cases were diagnosed postmortem. Invasive aspergillosis complicating severe dengue broadens the spectrum of viral-associated aspergillosis.
papers.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 侵袭性曲霉病通常发生在免疫功能低下的 宿主 中,但在病毒性疾病(包括登革热和 2019 年冠状病毒病)之后,人们越来越多地认识到侵袭性曲霉病。本文描述了 重症登革热 后传播性曲霉病的致命病例,并对这种关联进行了系统评价。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 在本次系统评价中,发现了另外 21 例登革热后侵袭性曲霉病病例(总数 = 22;中位年龄 36 岁,59% 男性),主要发生在亚洲。登革热 IgM 结果呈阳性,排除其他热带感染。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 一名先前健康的 25 岁女性出现发烧和多器官功能障碍。总体死亡率为63.6%;23%的病例是尸检确诊的。侵袭性曲霉病并发 重症登革热 拓宽了病毒相关曲霉病的范围。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 大多数患者患有 重症登革热 并伴有多器官功能障碍。15 例(68%)有肺部受累。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 尸检显示弥漫性肺泡损伤和广泛的侵袭性曲霉菌病,累及支气管、肺血管系统和心肌。尽管接受了重症监护,患者还是出现了进行性呼吸衰竭、难治性休克和急性肾损伤,最终死亡。

papers.source_body_en: Invasive aspergillosis typically occurs in immunocompromised hosts but has been increasingly recognized following viral illnesses, including dengue and coronavirus disease 2019. Herein, a fatal case of disseminated aspergillosis following severe dengue is described, and the association is systematically reviewed. A previously healthy 25-year-old woman presented with fever and multiorgan dysfunction. Dengue IgM results were positive, and other tropical infections were excluded. Despite intensive care, the patient developed progressive respiratory failure, refractory shock, and acute kidney injury and died. An autopsy revealed diffuse alveolar damage and extensive invasive aspergillosis involving the bronchi, pulmonary vasculature, and myocardium. In the present systematic review, 21 additional cases of invasive aspergillosis following dengue (total n = 22; median age 36 years, 59% male) were identified, predominantly in Asia. Fifteen cases (68%) had pulmonary involvement. Most patients had severe dengue with multiorgan dysfunction. The overall mortality was 63.6%; 23% of cases were diagnosed postmortem. Invasive aspergillosis complicating severe dengue broadens the spectrum of viral-associated aspergillosis.

papers.title: Community participation and operational lessons from implementing a protective coating as a novel vector control tool in dengue-endemic neighborhoods of Cúcuta and Los Patios, Colombia.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The control of Aedes-borne diseases (dengue, Zika, chikungunya, yellow fever) is a high public health priority in tropical and subtropical countries. The adoption of new vector control tools, such as protective coating (PC), requires understanding the social dynamics that influence their acceptance and feasibility. This study investigated the experiences and perspectives of diverse stakeholders involved in a vector control project in urban Colombia, with the aim of assessing community acceptance and operational feasibility. Insights gained are important for optimizing implementation and gauging the broader viability of innovative vector control strategies. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using focus group discussions and in-depth interviews with 70 key stakeholders, including community leaders ( n = 3), community volunteers ( n = 30), vector control staff ( n = 7), supervisors ( n = 5), and community residents ( n = 25). Data was collected after the intervention and analyzed using inductive thematic content analysis with open coding. Participation was voluntary and confidential. Results The protective coating was perceived as feasible and generally well accepted by the community. Facilitating factors included the involvement of community leaders, strong volunteer commitment, and effective coordination among institutions. Challenges such as trust issues, logistical constraints, and safety concerns were identified and addressed through adaptive strategies, including adjusted work schedules and strengthened communication. Conclusion Community involvement, effective communication, and adaptive management were key to the successful implementation of the protective coating and helped address logistical challenges. The lessons learned provide useful information for scaling up novel vector control approaches in similar urban settings in Latin America.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes qualitative evidence on the implementation of a protective coating (PC) as a vector control tool for Aedes-borne diseases in dengue-endemic urban neighborhoods of Colombia. The study engaged 70 stakeholders through focus groups and interviews, analyzed via thematic content analysis, and found the PC to be feasible and well accepted, with community leadership, volunteer engagement, and institutional coordination as critical facilitators. Challenges included logistical constraints, trust issues, and safety concerns, which were mitigated through adaptive strategies such as adjusted schedules and improved communication. The findings underscore the necessity of community participation, clear communication, and adaptive management for successfully scaling novel vector control interventions in comparable urban Latin American contexts.

papers.title: Temporal Modeling of Weekly Dengue Cases in Marikina City: A Time-Respecting Comparison of Classical, Machine Learning, and Deep Temporal Models
papers.abstract: Background Short-horizon dengue forecasting can support local preparedness, but model comparisons may be weakened by random splitting, information leakage, limited baseline testing, and insufficient out-of-time evaluation. This study developed a surveillance-only framework for forecasting weekly dengue incidence in Marikina City two weeks ahead. Methods Weekly records combined Marikina-filtered Department of Health–Epidemiology Bureau data from 2016–2020 with Marikina Epidemiology Surveillance Unit data from 2023–2025. The years 2021–2022 were excluded because the available records contained zero and three reported cases, respectively. Eight trained models—ARIMA, SARIMA, ETS, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, LSTM, and Temporal CNN—were compared with naïve and moving-average reference baselines. Target-year splits used 2024 for internal validation and model selection and 2025 as an out-of-time temporal holdout. Earlier observed 2025 case counts were permitted as causal inputs for forecasting later 2025 targets when they occurred before the relevant forecast origin. Mean absolute error was the primary metric, supported by root mean square error, coefficient of determination, feature importance, and incidence-class error analysis. Results The cleaned dataset contained 417 weekly observations and 8,263 reported cases. ARIMA was the strongest trained model during 2024 internal validation, although the two-week moving average and naïve baselines produced slightly lower errors. In the 2025 temporal holdout, LSTM achieved the most favorable metrics, with an MAE of 7.951, RMSE of 10.651, and R2 of 0.698, followed by ARIMA with an MAE of 8.652, RMSE of 11.686, and R2 of 0.636. Both achieved lower MAE than the naïve baseline. Tree-based models relied primarily on current incidence and two-week rolling summaries. All evaluated methods tended to underpredict outbreak-level weeks. Conclusions Surveillance-only forecasting was feasible under a leakage-safe temporal design. LSTM produced the strongest 2025 holdout metrics, while ARIMA remained an interpretable and computationally efficient alternative. Operational use should retain simple baselines, communicate uncertainty, and prioritize improved detection of rapid outbreak escalation.

LSTM produced the strongest 2025 holdout metrics, while ARIMA remained an interpretable and computationally efficient alternative. Operational use should retain simple baselines, communicate uncertainty, and prioritize improved detection of rapid outbreak escalation. 1 BACKGROUND Dengue remains a persistent public health concern in tropical and subtropical settings, where seasonal increases can rapidly strain clinical services, vector-control operations, and local surveillance teams [1, 3]. In densely populated urban areas, short-term increases in reported cases can affect staffing, bed capacity, diagnostics, medical supplies, and the timing of community interventions. City-level forecasts are therefore Page 2/19 potentially more actionable than national or regional summaries because local government units make many operational decisions at the city and barangay levels. Routine dengue surveillance produces chronologically ordered counts that contain temporal dependence. Recent incidence may represent ongoing transmission chains, reporting momentum, and the early development of outbreak waves [15, 16]. Classical time-series models capture this dependence directly through autoregressive, moving-average, trend, and seasonal components [4, 8, 19]. Machine-learning approaches instead transform the series into lag, rolling, change, trend, and calendar predictors, while deep temporal models learn representations from ordered case sequences [11–14, 17]. Forecasting credibility depends as much on experimental design as on algorithm choice. Random train-test splits violate temporal order, and preprocessing performed before the forecast cutoff may leak future information into model inputs. Time-respecting validation, causal feature construction, and comparison with simple persistence baselines are necessary to determine whether a trained model offers genuine predictive value [5–7]. These safeguards are particularly important for weekly dengue data, where adjacent observations are strongly correlated and naive forecasts can be difficult to beat. Existing dengue studies have demonstrated the value of autoregressive methods, tree ensembles, and recurrent neural networks, but performance varies across locations, forecast horizons, covariates, and evaluation designs [5, 13, 17, 20]. Local surveillance agencies may also lack consistently available meteorological, mobility, socioeconomic, or environmental variables. A surveillance-only design based on case counts and reporting dates can therefore provide a practical, reproducible baseline for data-constrained settings, although it cannot explain causal transmission mechanisms. This study developed and evaluated a leakage-safe, two-week-ahead forecasting framework for weekly dengue incidence in Marikina City. The objectives were to: (1) characterize trend, seasonality, autocorrelation, and lag behavior; (2) compare classical, machine-learning, and deep temporal models; (3) determine whether trained models improve on naive and moving-average baselines; and (4) identify the temporal predictors most strongly used by tree-based models. The principal contribution is a complete target-year evaluation design with 2024 reserved for internal model development and 2025 retained as a full unseen external holdout. 2 METHODS 2.1 Study Design and Setting The study used a quantitative predictive design focused on weekly dengue incidence in Marikina City, Philippines. The task was univariate, two-week-ahead regression: information observed at forecast origin t was used to predict the weekly dengue case count at t + 2. The study evaluated predictive accuracy rather than causal effects. No individual-level or personally identifiable health records were analyzed. 2.2 Data Sources and Eligibility The unified dataset combined two surveillance sources. Department of Health-Epidemiology Bureau records were filtered to retain only Marikina City observations from 2016–2020 [2]. More recent weekly records for 2023–2025 were obtained from the Marikina Epidemiology Surveillance Unit (MESU). The available 2021 record Page 3/19 contained zero cases and the 2022 record contained only three cases; both years were excluded because they were too sparse to support reliable lag, rolling-window, and sequence modeling. The cleaned series contained 417 weekly records and 8,263 reported cases. The training and development period included 313 weeks from 2016–2020 and 2023, with 4,999 cases. The 2024 internal-validation year contained 52 weeks and 1,867 cases. The 2025 external holdout contained 52 weeks and 1,397 cases. All three sets had no remaining duplicate dates or missing case values. The 2025 holdout included 15 low, 14 moderate, 16 high, and seven very high or outbreak-level weeks, providing a broader test than a partial-year holdout. Table 1 summarizes the resulting dataset structure and data quality by period. Table 1 Dataset structure and data quality Period Years Weeks Cases Use Historical segment 1 2016–2020 261 3,468 Training/development Excluded interval 2021–2022 - 0 and 3 Excluded for insufficient reporting Historical segment 2 2023 52 1,531 Training/development Internal validation 2024 52 1,867 Model and hyperparameter selection External holdout 2025 52 1,397 Final unseen evaluation Note. The training/development total was 313 weeks and 4,999 cases. Dashes indicate that the excluded records were not treated as a modeling segment. 2.3 Data Preparation and Temporal Segmentation Dates were converted to a standard datetime representation, case counts were converted to numeric form, invalid dates and missing targets were removed, negative values were bounded at zero, and records were sorted chronologically. The median interval between observations was checked to verify reporting frequency; the uploaded unified dataset was already weekly, so no additional aggregation was applied. Outbreak peaks were retained because they represented epidemiologically meaningful events rather than errors. A gap longer than 21 days defined a new continuous segment. This prevented lags, rolling statistics, expanding seasonal means, and deep-learning sequences from crossing the excluded 2021–2022 interval. Consequently, the last observation in 2020 was not treated as immediately adjacent to the first observation in 2023. Classical- model input was handled differently: the available observations before each cutoff were chronologically concatenated without explicit missing calendar positions. This did not introduce future targets, but it may have affected estimates of autocorrelation and seasonality and is treated as a limitation. 2.4 Exploratory Temporal Analysis and Feature Engineering The autocorrelation function (ACF), partial autocorrelation function (PACF), monthly and weekly seasonal profiles, and Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) were used to examine short-range persistence and annual structure [4, 19]. Because the strongest dependence occurred at early lags and annual recurrence was irregular, the machine-learning feature set emphasized recent history rather than direct 26- or 52-week lags. Page 4/19 For Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, each forecast origin included the current case count; lags at 1, 2, 4, 8, and 12 weeks; rolling means, sums, and standard deviations over 2, 4, 8, and 12 weeks; exponentially weighted means with spans of 4 and 8 weeks; one- and two-week differences; a bounded one- week percentage change; four- and eight-week local trend slopes; sine and cosine encodings of epidemiological week and month; a segment-local trend index; and expanding historical means for the same week and month. All transformations used only information available at or before the forecast origin. The supervised target was the case count two weeks later. LSTM and Temporal CNN inputs were constructed separately as segment-aware 12-week case sequences paired with the target at t + 2. ARIMA, SARIMA, and ETS operated on the chronological case-count series and did not use the engineered feature matrix. 2.5 Forecasting Models Five reference baselines were calculated without training: a naive forecast equal to the current observed case count and moving averages over the previous 2, 4, 8, and 12 weeks. Baselines were used only to establish the minimum practical standard and were not candidates for final trained-model selection. The classical models were ARIMA, SARIMA, and exponential smoothing (ETS). Candidate ARIMA orders (1,0,0), (2,0,0), and (3,0,0) were compared by 2024 rolling-origin MAE; ARIMA(3,0,0) was selected. SARIMA used order (1,0,0) with seasonal order (1,0,0,52). ETS used additive trend and additive seasonality with a 52-week period. ARIMA was repeatedly refitted at forecast origins, whereas SARIMA and ETS generated static full-horizon forecasts after fitting before the evaluation year [8–10]. The tree-based regressors were Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting. Candidate settings varied tree depth, leaf size, number of estimators, feature subsampling, learning rate, and subsampling ratio. Each candidate was evaluated with raw and log1p-transformed targets, and the configuration with the lowest 2024 MAE was selected. Random Forest reduces variance through bootstrap aggregation [11], while Gradient Boosting sequentially corrects residual error [12]. The LSTM used one recurrent layer with 32 hidden units followed by a linear output layer. The Temporal CNN used two one-dimensional convolutional layers with 32 channels per layer, kernel size 3, ReLU activations, adaptive average pooling, and a linear output. It is described as a Temporal CNN rather than a canonical dilated residual TCN because the implementation did not include explicit dilation or residual TCN blocks [14, 21]. Both neural models used training-derived standardization, Adam optimization with learning rate 0.001 and weight decay 0.0001, SmoothL1 loss, a maximum of 150 epochs, and early stopping with patience 12. Table 2 summarizes the input, selected configuration, and evaluation procedure for each trained model. Page 5/19 Table 2 Trained models and evaluation procedures Model Input and selected setup Evaluation procedure ARIMA Weekly series; selected order (3,0,0) Rolling-origin refitting in 2024 and 2025 SARIMA Weekly series; (1,0,0)(1,0,0,52) Static full-horizon forecast ETS Additive trend and seasonality; period 52 Static full-horizon forecast Decision Tree Engineered features; depth 3; leaf 5; log target Target-year validation and refit through 2024 Random Forest 200 trees; depth 5; max features 0.7; leaf 5 Target-year validation and refit through 2024 Gradient Boosting 100 trees; learning rate 0.05; depth 2 Target-year validation and refit through 2024 LSTM 12-week sequence; 32 hidden units Early stopping on 2024; final fit through 2024 Temporal CNN 12-week sequence; two Conv1D layers Early stopping on 2024; final fit through 2024 Note. Different forecast-generation procedures were retained by model family and are considered when interpreting direct comparisons. 2.6 Chronological Validation Observations were assigned according to the year of the forecast target rather than the year of the forecast origin. Targets occurring in 2023 or earlier formed the training and development set, targets occurring in 2024 formed the internal-validation set, and targets occurring in 2025 formed the out-of-time temporal holdout. This target-year assignment prevented forecasts originating near the end of one year from placing a target from the following year into an earlier split. The 2025 target values were excluded from ARIMA-order selection, machine-learning hyperparameter tuning, and initial neural-model validation. During the 2025 temporal holdout evaluation, earlier observed 2025 case counts could be used as historical inputs for later 2025 forecasts only when those observations occurred before the relevant forecast origin. Therefore, the 2025 targets remained held out from model development while forecasts were allowed to use causally available surveillance history. For the neural models, the 2024 validation period was used to select the architecture, training configuration, and number of training epochs. After these settings were fixed, the selected models were refitted using all eligible sequences through 2024 for the predetermined number of epochs without monitoring the 2025 holdout. The 2025 targets were then used only for final temporal evaluation. 2.7 Performance Measures and Interpretation Mean absolute error was treated as the primary operational metric because it directly represented the average weekly case-count error. Root mean square error was used to identify models with larger individual forecasting errors, while R2 provided supplementary information regarding variance explanation. Model conclusions were Page 6/19 based primarily on MAE and RMSE rather than on a custom percentage-accuracy measure. This evaluation approach follows established principles for assessing point forecasts using proper scoring rules [18]. Native impurity-based feature importance was extracted from the selected tree-based models. These scores describe how strongly predictors were used within each fitted model but do not represent causal relationships or permutation-based importance. Errors during the 2025 temporal holdout were also summarized according to incidence level. All analyses were performed in Python using pandas and NumPy for data handling, statsmodels for classical models, scikit-learn for tree regressors and evaluation, and PyTorch for neural models. Fixed random seeds and explicit configurations were used where supported. 3 RESULTS 3.1 Data Characteristics and Temporal Structure Annual totals varied substantially. The highest observed total was 1,867 cases in 2024, followed by 1,531 in 2023 and 1,397 in 2025. Weekly incidence included low-transmission periods and abrupt peaks, indicating that the series was not governed by a uniform annual trajectory. The feature-generation process produced 292 model-ready supervised observations: 189 with targets through 2023, 51 for 2024, and 52 for 2025. The deep- learning sequence dataset retained 52 targets in each evaluation year. Figure 1 shows the resulting weekly incidence series. Figure description: A weekly line plot covering 2016–2020 and 2023–2025 shows several irregular peaks, a gap for excluded 2021–2022 data, high activity in 2023–2024, and a lower but still variable full-year pattern in 2025. The ACF showed strong positive dependence at early lags, declining gradually across the following weeks. The PACF concentrated its strongest direct effects at lags 1 and 2. A weaker secondary ACF rise appeared near the annual range, but it was less pronounced than short-range persistence. These findings supported the reduced lag set and the emphasis on current incidence and rolling summaries. Figure 2 presents the ACF and PACF diagnostics described above.
